correctness.rationale: If a nonscalar a fixes a subspace of dimension j, then that subspace is a vector space over F_q(a), forcing [F_q(a):F_q] to divide gcd(4,j). Only j=2 permits degree 2, and the fixed two-spaces are then exactly the F_(q^2)-lines, in one orbit, all with stabilizer H=F_(q^2)^*/F_q^*. No nontrivial stabilizer of a positive-dimensional simplex is possible because its vertices have distinct types and it includes a 1- or 3-space. There are (q^2+1)(q^2+q+1) two-spaces, leaving q free orbits after removing the spread orbit. Direct flags counts give q^2+q+1 orbits for each of the three edge types and (q+1)(q^2+q+1) triangle orbits. Independently, Euler averaging over the type-preserving action gives chi=[1+q^6+q(q^2+1)]/[(q+1)(q^2+1)]=q^3-q^2+1: the identity contributes the building Euler characteristic and the q nonidentity elements in H each contribute the discrete spread. The simply connected building and Armstrong's ordinary orbit-space theorem give pi1=G_q/H, cyclic of order q^2+1 with no coprimality needed. H1 is its abelianization; H2 is the free top cellular kernel, with rank chi-1. I inspected verify_singer_building.py and VERIFICATION.md without running the script. Its recorded ranks and integral Smith factors at q=2,3 check the homology cases, not the nonabelian fundamental group or the quantifier over all fields.
